simple.meaning: רִמָּה (rimmâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a maggot (as rapidly bred ), literally or figuratively.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: רִמָּה (H7415) appears 7 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 16:24, with occurrences in Exodus, Job, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רִמָּה (H7415) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in רִמָּה (H7415) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: רִמָּה (rimmâh) / H7415 is traced through Exodus 16:24, Job 7:5, Job 17:14, Job 21:26 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a maggot (as rapidly bred ), literally or figuratively
definitions.full: H7415. rimmah רִמָּה noun feminine worm (cause and sign of decay ); — absolute ׳ר Exod 16:24 (P), Isa 14:11 (|| תּוֺלֵעָה ), Job 7:5 ; 17:14 ; 21:26 ; 24:20 all indicate corruption, feeding on dead, etc.; hyperb. of insignificant man 25:6 (|| תּוֺלֵעָה ).
definitions.rootNote: from 7426 in the sense of breeding (compare 7311 );

occurrences.englishText: They laid it up until the morning, as Moses ordered, and it didn’t become foul, and there were no worms in it.
My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust.
if I have said to corruption, ‘You are my father;’
They lie down alike in the dust.
How much less man, who is a worm,
Your pomp is brought down to Sheol,† Sheol is the place of the dead. with the sound of your stringed instruments. Maggots are spread out under you, and worms cover you.
